ucs.title: [LLM] Patchwork weaponized-document chain: Office → Equation Editor / mshta → BADNEWS side-loaded DLL
ucs.description: Hunts Patchwork's (Dropping Elephant / MONSOON / Hangover) signature initial-access chain where a spearphished RTF/Office lure exploits CVE-2017-11882 (Equation Editor) or CVE-2017-0199 / template injection and pivots through mshta/powershell to drop the BADNEWS implant via DLL search-order hijacking. The combination of an Office parent spawning eqnedt32.exe or a script/LOLbin is the actor's recurring exploitation fingerprint.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe")) AND (Processes.process_name IN ("eqnedt32.exe","mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"(?i)\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("eqnedt32.exe","mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildName  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ParentName in ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe")
| where ChildName in ("eqnedt32.exe","mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ucs.sigma_yaml:
title: Patchwork Office Lure Spawning Equation Editor or Script LOLBin
id: 6f1c4a2e-9b3d-4e7a-8c21-1f5d0a7b9c44
status: experimental
description: Detects Office applications spawning eqnedt32.exe or script/LOLbin children consistent with Patchwork (Dropping Elephant) CVE-2017-11882 / CVE-2017-0199 exploitation chains.
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\winword.exe'
      - '\excel.exe'
      - '\powerpnt.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\eqnedt32.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate Office add-ins or macros invoking script hosts (rare in modern hardened estates)
level: high
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1218
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\winword.exe OR *\WINWORD.EXE OR *\excel.exe OR *\EXCEL.EXE OR *\powerpnt.exe OR *\POWERPNT.EXE OR *\outlook.exe OR *\OUTLOOK.EXE) @Image:(*\eqnedt32.exe OR *\EQNEDT32.EXE OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\RegSvr32.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WScript.exe OR *\cscript.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\CertUtil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(winword|excel|powerpnt|outlook)\.exe/i
| ImageFileName=/(eqnedt32|mshta|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName], function=collect([CommandLine, SHA256HashData]))
ucs.rationale: Patchwork is one of the few crews whose intrusions consistently begin with CVE-2017-11882 Equation Editor and CVE-2017-0199/template-injection lures delivering BADNEWS — so an Office parent spawning eqnedt32.exe specifically (vs. generic powershell) is near-pathognomonic for this actor and very rare in benign telemetry. The LOLbin/script child set captures the actor's mshta and rundll32 side-load

ucs.title: [LLM] Patchwork BADNEWS dead-drop resolver C2 over legitimate web services
ucs.description: Hunts BADNEWS / QuasarRAT command resolution where Patchwork hides the real C2 address in posts on legitimate platforms (GitHub, WordPress/blog feeds, RSS/Feedburner, forums, Dynamic DNS) — a dead-drop resolver technique that is a hallmark of this actor's implants. Flags non-browser processes beaconing to these services.
ucs.splunk: | tstats `security_content_summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.app IN ("github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","feeds.feedburner.com","feedburner.com","wordpress.com","blogspot.com","pastebin.com")) AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe") by All_Traffic.dest All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.app All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)` | sort - lastTime
ucs.kql:
let DeadDropDomains = dynamic(["github.com","raw.githubusercontent.com","gist.githubusercontent.com","feeds.feedburner.com","feedburner.com","wordpress.com","blogspot.com","pastebin.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (DeadDropDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe","safari.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), Hits = count(), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl
| order by FirstSeen desc
ucs.sentinel_kql:
let DeadDropDomains = dynamic(["github.com","githubusercontent.com","feedburner.com","wordpress.com","blogspot.com","pastebin.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where isnotempty(Url)
| where Url has_any (DeadDropDomains) or DstHostname has_any (DeadDropDomains)
| where SrcProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","opera.exe")
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), Hits = count() by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, DstPortNumber
| order by FirstSeen desc
ucs.datadog_query: source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationHostname:(*github.com OR *githubusercontent.com OR *feedburner.com OR *wordpress.com OR *blogspot.com OR *pastebin.com)) -@Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\Chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\MsEdge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\Firefox.exe OR *\iexplore.exe OR *\IEXPLORE.EXE OR *\brave.exe OR *\opera.exe)
ucs.falcon_logscale_query:
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(github\.com|githubusercontent\.com|feedburner\.com|wordpress\.com|blogspot\.com|pastebin\.com)$/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|iexplore|opera)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())
| count > 1
ucs.rationale: The dead-drop resolver pattern — fetching the live C2 address from attacker-controlled posts on GitHub/blogs/RSS rather than hard-coding it — is a documented, distinctive trait of Patchwork's BADNEWS family (and its QuasarRAT usage), used to survive takedowns.
